questions.topic: Choosing an element for what it means rather than how it looks
questions.learningObjective: Choose between strong and b for importance
questions.stem: A report needs to mark text as important rather than merely bold.

answer.exemplar: Use strong because it marks importance, while b only draws attention without implying importance to assistive tools.

questions.explanation: Strong carries importance semantics, whereas b is presentational. Choosing by meaning preserves intent for assistive tools.

questions.topic: What a heading outline with a skipped level claims
questions.learningObjective: Decide whether to fix a skipped heading level
questions.stem: A report has h1, h2, h4 and the team can edit the markup.

options.text: Leave it because rendering is unaffected
Restyle the h4 to look like an h3
Insert the missing h3 level to repair the outline
Remove the h4 to avoid the gap

questions.explanation: The correct fix is to restore the missing level. Rendering and styling do not repair the outline gap.

questions.topic: The outer width under the initial box-sizing
questions.learningObjective: Compute outer width with border-box comparison
questions.stem: Under content-box, a box has width 160px, padding 12px, and border 3px.

answer.exemplar: The outer width is 190px because content-box adds both paddings and both borders: 160 + 12 + 12 + 3 + 3 equals 190.

questions.explanation: Content-box excludes padding and border from the declared width, so each side adds to the total. The box ends wider than 160px.
questions.hint: Add both sides of padding and border.

questions.topic: The content width under border-box sizing
questions.learningObjective: Compute content width for a border-box element
questions.stem: A border-box box declares width 160px with padding 12px and border 3px.

options.text: The content width is 160px because border-box keeps content fixed
The content width is 148px because only one side of padding counts
The content width is 190px because padding is added inside
The content width is 130px after removing padding and border

questions.explanation: Border-box includes padding and border in the declared width, so content is 160 minus 24 padding minus 6 border. The idea that content stays 160px is wrong.
questions.hint: Subtract both sides of padding and border.

questions.topic: What a heading outline with a skipped level claims
questions.learningObjective: Recognise that a skipped level does not invalidate HTML
questions.stem: A report has h1 then h3 and no h2 anywhere.

options.text: The document is valid but the outline has a gap
The document is invalid HTML and will not render
The h3 is promoted to h2 automatically
The browser inserts an empty h2

questions.explanation: Skipping a level does not make HTML invalid. The outline simply has a gap, which is a quality issue rather than a parse failure.
questions.hint: Invalid outline is not invalid HTML.

Acceptable if CSS later changes the size
options.misconception: thinks CSS can fix a wrong level

Not acceptable because h6 cannot be a heading

questions.explanation: Level reflects structure, not size. CSS handles size, so a level chosen for size misrepresents the document.
